A1.justification: Both PDFs describe xLSTM-Mixer with the same authors and core architecture. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original forecasting experiments, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses, including short-term PEMS results.

after.justification: The retained original experiments are supplemented by probabilistic forecasting, classification, efficiency measurements, and additional model analyses.

M1.justification: The three-stage forecasting backbone in Section 3 is retained. V3 adds a quantile-prediction head for probabilistic forecasting, a softmax classification head trained with cross-entropy, and an experimental extension of view mixing beyond two views. These are limited adaptations of the existing architecture.

E1.justification: V3 adds GIFT-Eval's heterogeneous univariate and multivariate probabilistic forecasting coverage and ten classification datasets, including Heartbeat, Handwriting, and SpokenArabicDigits. The seven original long-term forecasting datasets remain. V1's dedicated PEMS03/PEMS08 short-term point-forecasting comparison is removed.

E2.justification: The long-term comparison adds TimeMixer++, CycleNet, S-Mamba, Chimera, ModernTCN, Timer-XL, and MoiraiBase, while removing FEDFormer, Autoformer, and MICN from that experiment. iTransformer and TimesNet remain in v3's full Table 6. NLinear joins the lookback analysis. New comparisons also include GIFT-Eval forecasters such as TiRex and classification baselines such as DTW, XGBoost, and ROCKET.

E3.justification: V3 introduces probabilistic evaluation using MASE and quantile-based CRPS, classification evaluation using accuracy, and training-step time/memory measurements across lookback lengths. The plotted lookback sensitivity sweep extends from 1024 to 2048 steps. The original long-term horizons, MAE training objective, and hyperparameter search ranges remain unchanged; additional descriptions of baseline tuning do not establish rerunning the retained comparisons.

E4.justification: Table 3 expands from ten to fourteen configurations, testing mLSTM, LSTM, GRU, and DLinear substitutions. New analyses examine computational efficiency, Shapley-based cross-variate dependencies, random variate orderings, additional views, and dataset Hurst exponents. These directly investigate architectural and robustness questions left untested or deferred in v1. Existing token visualizations and hidden-dimension analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the same three seeds, 2021–2023. V3 extends uncertainty reporting with forecasting means and standard deviations in Table 7 and introduces Friedman tests, Conover post-hoc comparisons with Holm correction, and critical-difference diagrams. It restricts the long-term significance analysis to MSE at horizon 96 to avoid correlated horizons inflating significance.

E6.justification: Matched long-term entries and retained ablation configurations have unchanged numerical scores. Against the revised comparator set, xLSTM-Mixer's tabled wins change from 18 MSE/23 MAE to 11/16. New results include GIFT-Eval CRPS 0.510 and second place in Tables 2/8, classification accuracy of 74.1% versus ModernTCN's 74.2% in Table 14, and efficiency, permutation, view-count, and recurrent-cell results. The dedicated PEMS results disappear.

T1.justification: The forecasting formalization and core sLSTM equations are retained. Appendix B adds standard recurrence formulas and an intuitive state-tracking explanation; Appendix C documents standard evaluation metrics. These additions do not introduce substantive formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: V3 elevates low memory requirements into the abstract and introduction and explicitly claims the first combination of recurrent forecasting with mixing architectures. Its conclusion expands demonstrated applicability to probabilistic forecasting and classification, previously outside the established contributions. The reported long-term dominance changes from 41/56 to 27/56 cases against the revised comparisons.

C2.justification: V3 develops a state-tracking explanation for choosing sLSTM, interprets cross-variate attribution and ordering experiments, and explains why excessive lookback can hurt short-horizon forecasts. It adds conclusions about probabilistic transfer and extra views. Limitations now explicitly address irregular or missing timestamps, channel-dependent resource scaling, and attribution difficulties, extending v1's brief channel-count limitation.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents 32-bit training, GluonTS integration, Captum and scikit-posthocs usage, baseline-result provenance, and the zero-baseline/horizon-aggregation procedure for Shapley attribution. The original hardware, optimizer, training budget, search ranges, and code-access information remain substantially unchanged. These additions mainly improve documentation rather than establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands positioning to distinguish state-space, mixing, and pretrained forecasting approaches, discussing works such as Mamba, Chimera, Chronos, Moirai, and Timer-XL. Concurrent xLSTM research and newer mixing architectures are incorporated. The explicit first recurrent–mixing combination claim also sharpens the stated relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized into separate forecasting, GIFT-Eval, classification, model-analysis, and ablation sections. Appendices are restructured into A–J; societal-impact discussion and token visualizations move there, and a NeurIPS checklist is added. The introduction, conclusion, headings, and explanatory passages receive substantial revision, although much of the core method exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 adds an introductory efficiency figure, critical-difference diagrams, attribution heatmaps, and tables for uncertainty, GIFT-Eval, permutations, extra views, and classification. The ablation table gains columns and separates recurrent type from recurrence order. Earlier sensitivity plots are combined into Figure 4, with a revised logarithmic lookback axis; token plots move to the appendix. Title, author, header, and page styling also change.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the empirical justification: controlled recurrent-cell substitutions test the central sLSTM choice, and ordering/view experiments address questions deferred in v1. Updated comparators, measured efficiency, significance analyses, and broader task evaluation make the claims more assessable. There are localized reporting defects: Table 7's TimeMixer averages conflict with Tables 1/6, and GIFT-Eval prose disagrees with its tables on some CRPS values. These defects and removal of the dedicated PEMS comparison do not outweigh the stronger validation and clearer limitations.
